name: Geneva
tagline: Diplomacy, watchmaking and a lake framed by Mont Blanc
whenBlurb: May to September is the season for the lake and the Alps; come in April for Watches and Wonders or mid-December for L'Escalade, and skip the cold, grey heart of winter.

ourTake.lede: Geneva is a working international city more than a holiday town, and it repays travellers who lean into the lake, the watchmaking and the surrounding Alps rather than expecting Old-World charm on every corner. Do the old town and a lake crossing, use the city as a base for Mont Blanc and the vineyards of Lavaux, and time a serious meal or a watch appointment if that's your interest. It is expensive and reserved, so keep the pace unhurried.
ourTake.comeIf: You want a calm, polished lakeside base for watches, wellness and easy Alpine day-trips.
ourTake.skipIf: You want buzz, nightlife or a bargain; Geneva is quiet and expensive.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: Beau-Rivage Genève
items.description: The city's grande dame since 1865, fifth-generation family-owned, lake-facing, and quite simply the Geneva address.

items.name: The Woodward, Auberge Resorts Collection
items.description: Geneva's only all-suite palace, a Belle Époque landmark reimagined by Pierre-Yves Rochon, facing the lake and Mont Blanc.

items.name: Four Seasons Hotel des Bergues Genève
items.area: Rive Droite / Les Bergues (Quai des Bergues)
items.description: Geneva's oldest grand hotel, open since 1834, a neoclassical house on the Rhône with Four Seasons polish.

items.name: Mandarin Oriental, Geneva
items.area: Rive Droite / on the Rhône (Quai Turrettini)
items.description: Mandarin Oriental precision on the riverbank, one of only two Forbes Five-Star houses in the city.

items.name: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel de la Paix, Geneva
items.description: An 1865 lakefront landmark reborn under The Ritz-Carlton, grand, contemporary and squarely on the water.

items.name: La Réserve Genève Hotel & Spa
items.area: Bellevue / lakefront, just north of the city
items.description: A Jacques Garcia-designed lakeside resort in its own park, a colonial-safari fantasy a short drive from the centre.

items.name: Hôtel President Wilson, a Luxury Collection Hotel
items.description: A diplomat's favourite on the lake, home to the Royal Penthouse, long reputed the most expensive hotel suite in the world.

items.name: Hôtel d'Angleterre
items.description: An intimate Red Carnation townhouse on the lake, English warmth and a famous piano bar, at a gentler scale than the palaces.

items.name: Hôtel Métropole Genève
credentials: The Leading Hotels of the World
items.description: A family-owned Belle Époque house on the left-bank lakefront, dignified, discreet and quietly grand.

items.name: Hôtel Les Armures
items.description: A 17th-century house at the very heart of the medieval Old Town, history, stone and quiet a step from the cathedral.

items.name: InterContinental Genève
items.area: Grand-Saconnex / near the UN and airport
items.description: The city's diplomatic-summit hotel, large, capable and close to the Palais des Nations and the airport.

items.name: The Jet d'Eau
items.description: Geneva's signature: a 140-metre plume of lake water shooting up from the harbour, visible from across the city and lit at night. Ask your driver to time an evening lakeside walk along the Quai Gustave-Ador so the children see it catch the last light.

items.name: CGN Belle Époque paddle-steamer cruise
items.description: Board one of the fleet of restored 1900s-era steamers at the Jardin Anglais or Mont-Blanc landing and glide past vineyards, châteaux and the Alps with a private table for lunch. The unhurried pace and top-deck views suit a multi-generational family, and the galley will manage vegetarian requests with notice.

items.name: Bains des Pâquis
items.description: The beloved public bathing pier reaching into the lake beside the Jet d'Eau, with wooden decks, a sauna and hammam in winter, and a famously good fondue in the little buvette. Unpretentious and thoroughly local, it is where Geneva actually relaxes.

items.name: Jardin Anglais & the Flower Clock
items.description: The lakeside promenade where Geneva's most photographed emblem, the Horloge Fleurie, is planted in thousands of live blooms that change with the season, its second hand the longest in the world. A gentle, pram-friendly stroll right by the Jet d'Eau.

items.name: Île Rousseau
items.description: A leafy islet in the middle of the Rhône, reached by a short footbridge, with the seated statue of philosopher Jean-Jacques Rousseau under old trees and swans on the water. A quiet green pause in the very heart of the city.

items.name: St Pierre Cathedral & its towers
items.description: The Old Town's Reformation-era cathedral where John Calvin preached, its climbable towers rewarding the effort with the finest rooftop panorama of the lake, the Alps and the tiled roofs below. Beneath it, the archaeological site reveals Roman and early-Christian layers.

items.name: Place du Bourg-de-Four
items.description: Geneva's oldest square, a sloping cobbled space of cafés, a central fountain and antique shops that has been a marketplace since Roman times. The natural spot to sit with a coffee and watch Old Town life unfold.

items.name: Maison Tavel
items.description: The oldest private house in Geneva, a 12th-century stone mansion now a museum of the city's history, whose highlight is the vast Magnin relief model of 1850s Geneva before its ramparts fell. A calm, uncrowded window into how the city grew.

items.name: The Reformation Wall
items.description: A 100-metre monument set into the old ramparts of Parc des Bastions, its five-metre statues of Calvin, Farel, Bèze and Knox marking Geneva's role as the 'Protestant Rome'. The surrounding park has giant chess boards the children can play on.

items.name: Parc des Bastions
items.description: The elegant park at the foot of the Old Town, home to the Reformation Wall, the University of Geneva's founding buildings and rows of giant open-air chess sets. Shaded, central and made for an easy afternoon.

items.name: Patek Philippe Museum
items.description: A private, hushed temple to watchmaking assembled by the Stern family, spanning five centuries of timepieces, enamels and automata across four floors, with Patek's own masterpieces on the top. Essential for the collector and a discreet, world-class hour for anyone with an interest in horology.

items.name: Rue du Rhône watch and jewellery boutiques
items.description: Geneva's golden mile: the flagship maisons of Patek Philippe, Rolex, Vacheron Constantin, Cartier and their peers line the Rue du Rhône and adjacent lanes. Private appointments and after-hours viewings are the norm for serious clients, arranged discreetly.

items.name: Cité du Temps
items.description: A free exhibition space on a bridge over the Rhône dedicated to time and Swiss watchmaking, with the Planet Swatch collection and rotating horological shows. A light, engaging counterpoint to the grand watch museums, right in the centre.

items.name: International Red Cross & Red Crescent Museum
items.description: A moving, superbly designed museum opposite the UN telling the story of humanitarian action through three chambers on defending dignity, restoring family links and reducing natural risks. Sober and powerful, and a reminder of why Geneva matters to the world.

items.name: Palais des Nations (UN Geneva)
items.description: The European headquarters of the United Nations, its grand halls and the ceiling of the Human Rights room open to guided visits set within a park roamed by peacocks. Bring passports; a private guide smooths the security and brings the diplomacy alive.

items.name: The Broken Chair
items.description: A 12-metre wooden chair with a shattered leg standing before the UN, a stark monument against landmines and cluster bombs. It stops every visitor for a moment and photographs beautifully against the flags.

items.name: CERN Science Gateway
items.description: The Renzo Piano-designed visitor centre of the world's great particle-physics laboratory, with free interactive exhibitions on the universe, the quantum world and the Large Hadron Collider. Genuinely thrilling for curious teenagers and science-minded travellers; registration is free but required.

items.name: Musée d'art et d'histoire (MAH)
items.description: One of Switzerland's largest museums, an encyclopaedic collection of fine art, antiquities and armour from Hodler and Corot to Egyptian and Roman treasures. Vast and serene, with an inflatable art installation currently animating its courtyard.

items.name: Conservatoire et Jardin botaniques (Botanical Garden)
items.description: Twenty-eight free hectares of themed gardens, greenhouses, an arboretum and a small animal park on the lake's edge, kept to a high standard. An easy, restful outing that works for grandparents and small children alike.

items.name: Carouge
items.description: Geneva's 'little Italy', a Sardinian-built quarter of low pastel houses, leafy inner courtyards, artisan workshops and independent cafés often called the city's Greenwich Village. The place to browse jewellers and design studios far from the tourist run, then linger over lunch on a shaded square.

items.name: Parc La Grange & its rose garden
items.description: The city's most beautiful park, an 18th-century estate above the lake whose historic Roseraie holds thousands of rose bushes in hundreds of varieties, at their peak in June. Free summer concerts play in the grounds.

items.name: Parc des Eaux-Vives
items.description: An elegant lakeside park adjoining La Grange, with sweeping lawns, old trees and long views to the Jet d'Eau and Mont Blanc. Its 18th-century villa houses a fine restaurant, making it a natural pairing with a garden walk.

items.name: Mont Salève cable car
items.description: A five-minute cable-car ride up 'Geneva's balcony' on the French side to 1,100 metres, with the whole city, the lake and, on clear days, Mont Blanc laid out below. Passports needed; the summit has walking trails and a viewpoint restaurant.

items.name: Plainpalais flea market
items.description: One of Europe's largest flea markets, sprawling across the great open plaza every Wednesday and Saturday, from watch parts and vintage Swiss enamel to furniture and curiosities. A treasure hunt for the collector's eye, best in the morning.

items.name: Villa Diodati (exterior)
items.description: The lakeside mansion above Geneva where Mary Shelley conceived Frankenstein during the stormy summer of 1816 with Byron. Privately owned so only the exterior and surrounding paths can be seen, but the literary aura and Cologny's grand villas make it a rewarding detour by car.

items.name: Auer chocolatier
items.description: A family chocolate house since 1939, tucked in the shopping streets and famed for its amandes princesses and delicate pralines. A small, authentic institution for a discreet gift or a private tasting.

items.name: Favarger chocolate
items.description: Geneva's historic chocolate maker, run by the same family since 1826, whose Avelines and Nougalines are local legends; its lakeside Carouge factory can be visited. An easy, crowd-pleasing stop for the family that travels with a sweet tooth.

items.name: Le Chat-Botté
items.description: The Michelin-starred dining room of the grand Beau-Rivage hotel, refined French cuisine with a lake terrace and a dedicated vegetarian tasting menu. The natural choice for a formal family dinner where the setting matters as much as the plate.

items.name: Old Town antiquarian and gallery lanes
items.description: The steep cobbled streets around Grand-Rue and Rue des Granges hide antiquarian booksellers, art galleries and Rousseau's birthplace at No. 40. A slow, elegant amble through the city's most historic quarter.

items.name: Quai du Mont-Blanc grand-hotel promenade
items.description: The stately waterfront where Geneva's palace hotels line up facing the Jet d'Eau and the Brunswick Monument, with the flower-lined Bains-Anglais steps and lake views. A classic evening stroll from the Beau-Rivage and the Four Seasons doorsteps.

items.name: Lausanne & the Olympic Museum
items.description: The Olympic capital across the lake, its lakeside Olympic Museum set in sculpture gardens tracing the Games from antiquity to now, a hit with children. Pair it with Ouchy's waterfront and the medieval cathedral in the upper town.

items.name: Lavaux vineyard terraces
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Lavaux, Vineyard Terraces
items.description: Steep, ancient stone-walled vineyards cascading to the lake between Lausanne and Montreux, monk-built from the 11th century and among the most beautiful winescapes in Europe. Arrange a private cellar tasting of the rare Chasselas whites, or ride the little Lavaux Express train through the rows.

items.name: Montreux & Chillon Castle
items.description: The Riviera-like resort town on the lake's east end, its promenade lined with palms and the Freddie Mercury statue, leading to the storybook Château de Chillon rising straight from the water. The 1,000-year-old castle that inspired Byron is a highlight for every generation.

items.name: Annecy
items.description: The 'Venice of the Alps' across the border, a jewel of flower-draped canals, a lakeside old town and turquoise water framed by peaks. A relaxed, walkable day of markets, gelato and boat rides; passports required for the border.

items.name: Chamonix & Aiguille du Midi
items.description: The legendary alpine town at the foot of Mont Blanc, from where the Aiguille du Midi cable car climbs to 3,842 metres and a glass 'Step into the Void' box over the glaciers. Unforgettable high-mountain drama within a day of Geneva; a private driver makes the border and timings effortless.

items.name: Gruyères
items.description: A perfectly preserved medieval hilltop village with a hilltop castle, famous for its AOP cheese dairy and the nearby Cailler chocolate factory at Broc. Cheese, chocolate and a fairy-tale walled town in one outing that delights children and adults.

items.name: Salève and lakeside private helicopter flight
items.description: A scenic helicopter transfer or flightseeing loop over the lake, the vineyards and the Mont Blanc massif, arranged from Geneva airport. The most spectacular way to grasp the geography, and a memorable treat for a family celebration.

items.name: MEG, Musée d'ethnographie de Genève
credentials: European Museum of the Year Award winner (2017)
items.description: An award-winning ethnography museum in striking modern architecture, showing world cultures through a collection of over 70,000 objects. Thoughtful, uncrowded and a strong wet-weather alternative to the lake.

items.name: Fondation Baur, Museum of Far Eastern Art
items.description: A discreet town-mansion museum of Chinese and Japanese art, jades, ceramics and Samurai swords, one of Europe's finest such collections. A serene, little-known gem for a quiet cultured hour.

items.name: Ariana Museum (ceramics & glass)
items.description: A palatial 19th-century villa in the UN's park devoted to a thousand years of glass and ceramics, from Sèvres porcelain to contemporary work. Beautiful architecture, free entry to the permanent collection and a peaceful park setting.

items.name: Barbier-Mueller Museum
items.description: A small, exquisite private museum of tribal and ancient art from Africa, Oceania and the Americas, superbly lit and curated in the heart of the Old Town. For the connoisseur, one of the world's great collections of its kind.

items.name: Bodmer Foundation library & museum
credentials: UNESCO Memory of the World collection
items.description: A jaw-dropping private library above the lake at Cologny holding a Gutenberg Bible, Shakespeare folios and papyrus fragments among world literature's treasures. A cultural pilgrimage for bibliophiles, in one of Geneva's grandest residential enclaves.

items.name: L'Atelier Robuchon
items.description: Geneva's only two-star table, the late Joël Robuchon's counter concept, exact and theatrical, around an open kitchen.

items.name: Domaine de Châteauvieux
items.description: Philippe Chevrier's country auberge among the vineyards, a Geneva institution, and GaultMillau's highest-scored table in the region.

items.name: Bayview by Michel Roth
items.area: Hôtel President Wilson, Rive Droite / lakefront
items.description: Refined French cooking under Michel Roth and Danny Khezzar, the lake and the Alps filling the windows.

items.name: Il Lago
items.area: Four Seasons Hotel des Bergues, Rive Droite / Les Bergues
items.description: Refined northern-Italian cooking in the Four Seasons' gilded room, classical, generous and beautifully served.

items.name: Fiskebar
items.area: The Ritz-Carlton Hotel de la Paix, Rive Droite / lakefront
items.description: A Nordic seafood enclave inside the Ritz-Carlton, clean, precise, sea-led cooking with a Scandinavian hand.

items.name: Rasoi by Vineet
items.area: Mandarin Oriental, Rive Droite / on the Rhône
items.description: Vineet Bhatia's evolved, refined Indian cooking, a rare starred Indian table, on the riverbank at the Mandarin Oriental.

items.name: Tsé Fung
items.description: Switzerland's only Michelin-starred Chinese restaurant, Cantonese refinement in Jacques Garcia's lakeside resort.

items.name: Le Cigalon
items.description: The Bessire family's seafood room, first-class fish flown from Roscoff and Audierne, cooked with flawless craft for nearly thirty years.

items.name: La Chaumière
items.description: Serge Labrosse's creative, modern cooking in a converted farmhouse, refined food in an easy country setting.

items.name: L'Aparté
items.description: Armel Bedouet's tiny fifteen-seat room, intimate, precise, produce-led fine dining for a handful of guests.

items.name: La Micheline
items.description: Andres Arocena's bright, seasonal bistronomy, a young star at the new Eaux-Vives station quarter.

items.name: Tosca
items.description: Ivan Baretti's precise Tuscan cooking, Arpège-trained technique in an intimate Eaux-Vives room.

items.name: Windows
items.description: Well-crafted French cooking with the Jet d'Eau and Mont Blanc framed in the window, a lovely lakefront room.

items.name: Osteria della Bottega
items.description: Seasonal Italian with handmade pasta at its heart, an open kitchen and chic industrial room in the Old Town.

items.name: Le Dorian
items.description: A well-priced newcomer with real flavour and craft, the kind of honest, refined cooking the Bib rewards.

items.name: Natürlich
items.description: Sustainable, produce-led cooking on the river, fresh, local ingredients handled with a light, honest touch.

items.name: Leopard Bar, Hôtel d'Angleterre
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN One-Key, Forbes 4-Star hotel, a Geneva institution
items.description: A clubby, low-lit lakefront piano bar, live jazz most nights and one of the city's most characterful drinks.

items.name: Le Bar des Bergues, Four Seasons
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Two-Key, Forbes 5-Star hotel
items.description: The Four Seasons' elegant bar, a considered cocktail in one of the city's most polished rooms.

items.name: Atrium Bar, Mandarin Oriental
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN One-Key, Forbes 5-Star hotel
items.description: A stylish riverside bar at the Mandarin Oriental, accomplished cocktails with the group's signature service.

items.name: Le Bar, The Woodward
credentials: Inside a MICHELIN Three-Key hotel (Auberge Resorts Collection)
items.description: An intimate, jewel-box bar inside the city's most exclusive hotel, discreet, dressed-up and beautifully made.

plan.heading: 3 days in Geneva, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

days.label: Day 1
days.title: The lake and the old town

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Jet d'Eau and the flower clock, then up into the Vieille Ville to St. Pierre Cathedral and the quiet Place du Bourg-de-Four.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The watchmaking rooms of the Patek Philippe Museum, then the Grand Rue for antiquarian bookshops.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at the Hôtel Beau-Rivage's Le Chat-Botté, a Geneva institution overlooking the lake.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Palais des Nations and the Red Cross Museum for the humanitarian city.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Cross into the Genevois vineyards for a tasting at a Dardagny or Satigny domaine.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Bayview by Michel Roth in the Hôtel President Wilson, two Michelin stars on the water.

days.label: Day 3
days.title: The far shore and the mountain

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A morning at the Fondation Baur for its Chinese and Japanese collections, or the CERN visit if science calls.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: The cable car up the Salève on the French side for lunch and the view back across the lake to Mont Blanc.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A quieter last dinner at the Domaine de Châteauvieux in Satigny, a two-star inn among the vines.

items.name: Vieille Ville (Old Town)
items.description: The hilltop historic core around the cathedral, cobbled and calm; suits those wanting the most characterful base.

items.name: Rive Gauche / Eaux-Vives
items.description: The lakeside left bank of parks, boutiques and good tables; suits travellers who want the water and the shopping close.

items.name: Pâquis
items.description: The lively, mixed quarter near the lake baths with the best-value eating; suits those wanting energy and range over polish.

events.name: Fête de l'Escalade
events.note: Geneva's beloved festival marking the 1602 defeat of Savoy, with torch-lit processions in period dress and chocolate cauldrons.

events.name: Fête de la Musique
events.note: Three days of free concerts across squares and courtyards throughout the old town for the summer solstice.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: The Right Bank (Rive Droite), near the Beau-Rivage and Four Seasons, puts you on the lake and by the finest maisons; Geneva is quiet and private by nature, which suits a discreet stay.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Geneva Airport (GVA) sits minutes from the city and lake, and a private car handles the short, discreet transfer to your hotel or lakeside residence.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver is the natural choice; the quais and old town reward walking, and a private boat is the elegant way to cross or explore Lac Léman.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: Excellent throughout; an eSIM works on arrival and covers the wider Lake Geneva region including nearby France.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Swiss francs (CHF), though euros are often accepted near the border; cards work everywhere and tipping is light, round up or leave a little for good service.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: May to September is mild and green along the lake with long evenings; winters are damp, foggy and cold, and November is the flattest month to avoid.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: No direct flights from India; the cleanest routing is via Zurich on SWISS, or via a European or Gulf hub, roughly 11-13 hours door to door with one stop. Fly SWISS through Zurich for the smoothest connection and a single-carrier baggage handover.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No vaccinations needed beyond routine; safety is excellent, on par with the rest of Switzerland. Tap water is clean and drinkable throughout the city.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Vegetarian and Jain needs are well understood in a cosmopolitan, diplomatic city. Good Indian and pure-vegetarian options exist, and most kitchens will adapt for Jain diners with notice.
